solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

E012-01.notes: Possessive pronoun 'its' (library's staff); it's = it is, their mismatches singular library, its' is not a word.

E012-02.notes: Interrupting list must be closed with a second dash to match the opening dash; A mixes dash and comma, B creates comma confusion with the list, C leaves the dash unclosed.

E012-03.notes: 'librarian Dana Whitfield' is the appositive to 'founder', set off by commas on both sides; no comma between title and name (restrictive). C drops closing comma; D's dash is unbalanced.

E012-04.notes: Beekeeping/honey is irrelevant to the seed library; B misstates what the sentence does, D's contradiction is false.

E012-05.notes: Faulty comparison: tomatoes must be compared with tomatoes, not packets. B still compares to packets; C uses singular 'that' for plural tomatoes.

E012-06.notes: 'In practice' pairs with 'In theory' to signal contrast; the others signal similarity, cause, or example.

E012-07.notes: Comma splice; a colon properly introduces the rule that explains 'a simple rule'. C is run-on; D 'rule; and seeds' is ungrammatical.

E012-08.notes: Hypothetical (counterfactual) conditional with 'would double' requires past-tense 'returned' in the if-clause; C 'would return' in the if-clause is a common trap.

E012-09.notes: Subject is singular 'variety' (of beans... that borrowers have brought back), so 'has'; intervening plural nouns are the trap. D creates a fragment.

E012-10.notes: Sentence adds a weightier criticism (rents) that sets up Ibarra 'takes these concerns seriously'; A overstates ('proves'), C/D misdescribe it.

flags: minor: in D, 'it' has no clear antecedent in the preceding sentence (nearest nouns are mango/stall/something else); 'the market' would be cleaner
minor: D is the longest choice (length cue)
E012-11.notes: Only D returns to the market serving neighbors; A is a detail about Ibarra, B is expansion, C shifts to the library.
